name: Carnation Pink
lede: Carnation pink is a soft, light pink named for the carnation flower; the related word carnation had an older sense in painters' flesh tints.

sections.title: Flower and flesh
sections.body:
In Baty's table of reds and browns, carnation pink (*Dianthus caryophyllus*) is listed as a plant example of carmine red, alongside the raspberry and the cockscomb, with oriental ruby as the mineral example [1].

In the pigment trade, *carnation* was also a loose term for mixtures of pigments used for flesh tints rather than any one pigment [2]. The Compendium quotes Harris (1704-10) using the word for the bare flesh of a painted figure, and calls a well-colored carnation a sign of a good painter [2]. So an old painter's carnation was skin, and a modern carnation pink is a flower. See also [[carnation]], [[flesh-pink]], [[raspberry]] and [[pink]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole [3].
